steps.name: QC and log2-TPM preparation
steps.question: Are the 12 skin samples cleanly aligned between tpm.csv and metadata.csv, are log2(TPM+1) distributions comparable across the 6 lesional and 6 control samples, and does PCA show a coherent condition effect without outliers that would invalidate a simple two-group contrast?
steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-v2-without-tpm-input-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/abundance/tpm.csv (12,000 gene symbols x 13 columns, first column gene symbol) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-tpm-input-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 2, condition column). Verify sample IDs match 1:1 between the two files and that condition is exactly 6 lesional vs 6 control. Compute log2(TPM+1). Check gene-symbol uniqueness/duplicates and any zero/negative or missing TPM values. Produce: per-sample log2TPM box/density plots, a sample-to-sample Pearson/Spearman correlation heatmap, and a PCA (top PCs colored by condition). No batch term is fitted (single batch). Report the fraction of genes expressed at mean TPM>=1 in each group, which feeds the pre-test filter of the DE step. No reference data needed.
acceptance_criteria: Sample IDs in tpm.csv and metadata.csv match exactly 1:1 with 6 lesional and 6 control
Per-sample distribution plots, correlation heatmap, and PCA (PC1/PC2 colored by condition) are produced and saved
A written QC verdict states whether any sample is an outlier and whether PCA separates lesional from control
Counts of duplicate gene symbols and missing/invalid TPM values are reported

steps.name: Lesional vs control differential expression (limma)
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between psoriasis lesional skin and control skin, ranked by moderated t-statistic with BH FDR<0.05?
steps.description: On log2(TPM+1) values from T1S1, keep genes with mean TPM>=1 in at least one group (report how many of the 12,000 survive), fit a limma linear model with design ~0+condition, form the lesional-vs-control contrast, and apply eBayes with trend=TRUE. Output the full ranked table (gene symbol, mean TPM per group, log2FC, t, P.Value, BH-adjusted adj.P.Val), the DE call set at adj.P.Val<0.05 with an additional |log2FC|>=1 emphasis tier, a volcano plot, an MA-style plot (log2FC vs mean log2TPM), and a heatmap of the top 50 DE genes with condition annotation. As a biological sanity check, report where canonical psoriasis markers (S100A7, S100A8, S100A9, DEFB4, IL36G) rank, including whether any are absent from the 12,000-gene table. State explicitly that because only TPM was delivered, DESeq2/edgeR count models were not applicable and results are approximate; the effect-size ranking is the primary output. No reference data needed.
acceptance_criteria: Full ranked results table for all filter-surviving genes with log2FC, moderated t, P.Value, BH adj.P.Val
DE call set at adj.P.Val<0.05 reported with the |log2FC|>=1 tier, plus a volcano, MA-style plot, and top-50 heatmap
Number of genes retained by the TPM>=1 filter is reported against the 12,000 input
Ranks of S100A7/S100A8/S100A9/DEFB4/IL36G reported, noting any absent symbols
A limitations note records that TPM-only input precludes count-based models

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are shifted in lesional vs control skin, given the ranked DE gene list from T1S2?
steps.description: Run gene-set enrichment with fgsea on the full moderated-t ranking from T1S2 against the provisioned WikiPathways human GMT (HGNC gene symbols, ~341 KB; readable set name = first field split on '%'), plus a classic over-representation test (clusterProfiler or equivalent) on the adj.P.Val<0.05 DE gene set with the T1S2 gene universe as background. Output an fgsea table (pathway, size, NES, pval, BH padj) sorted by padj, a bar/dot plot of the top enriched pathways with leading-edge sizes, and a short summary of immune/keratinization pathways (e.g. psoriasis, IL-17/keratinocyte pathways if present) among the hits. If the GMT file is absent or fails to parse, report the over-representation results alone and state the gap rather than failing the step.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea results table with pathway, size, NES, pval, BH padj for all parsed WikiPathways human sets
Over-representation analysis on the DE set using the T1S2 gene universe as background
Plot of top enriched pathways by NES/padj
Written summary naming the leading immune/keratinization pathways and their direction (positive = up in lesional)
Explicit note if the WikiPathways GMT had to be skipped

plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control DE from TPM (limma)
plan.analytical_narrative: The delivered data is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample gene-level TPM table from Salmon with a 12x2 metadata file (6 psoriasis lesional vs 6 control skin, unpaired, single batch); no raw counts or quantification directories exist. That constraint rules out negative-binomial count models (DESeq2/edgeR), which require integer counts, and makes limma on log2(TPM+1) with empirical-Bayes moderation the defensible DE approach for this dataset. The plan therefore: (1) QC the TPM matrix — verify sample/condition alignment, log2-transform, check distributional consistency and PCA structure for outliers or a condition-vs-batch confound (single batch, so no batch term is fitted); (2) run the lesional-vs-control contrast with limma (trend=TRUE to accommodate the intensity-dependent variance typical of abundance data), ranking all genes by moderated t and calling significance at BH FDR<0.05, reporting the full table, volcano, top-gene heatmap, and a sanity overlap with canonical psoriasis markers (S100A7, S100A8, S100A9, DEFB4, IL36G); (3) interpret the ranked gene list by pathway-level enrichment (fgsea over the moderated-t ranking against the provisioned WikiPathways human GMT, plus over-representation of the significant gene set) so the DE result is read in biological context rather than as a bare gene list. All steps report the TPM-only limitation: without counts, tests operate on already-normalized, compositional abundances and cannot model count precision, so p-values should be treated as approximate and the ranking of effect sizes as the primary output.
